answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The orchard multiplier is published, charged in crystal, and island lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4448 identities would post 3853 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
